title: Unless
program_note:
this piece is based on  what  i  call  a  “fold-out form”:   the  outer  portion  is   a simple rondo form, exploring a

multi-octave 28-note “mode,” within  which  a  large  middle  section  is  embedded,  containing suggestions of

several other modes.  since  this  large  middle  section  expands  the  time  in the piece, inexact mirror

images or formal repeats  allow  it  to  both  expand  and  compress time.    to   create a constantly-swirling

and churning surface,  even  seemingly-slow  sections  have  great  energy,  with driving sixteenth-note

motion.

about 8-½ minutes in duration, the outer section of   the piece is about 5-½

minutes long  and the inner section adds an additional 3 minutes.

it was composed for    and    commissioned    in    early    Autumn,    2014    by    the Moscow Contemporary Music    Ensemble, and is dedicated to the  wonderfully-talented  individual  members  of the Ensemble.

David S. Lefkowitz

Los Angeles, CA

13 May, 2015

As a “fold-out” piece, Un- (time) -less exists in two versions:  there is a simple, short version (as represented by the drawing on the left), and a longer, more complex version with the outer sections “folded out” to reveal a middle section (as represented by the drawing on the right).  The important feature of a “fold-out” piece is that the folded-out version of the piece be perceived as different from the unfolded version—that is, that the presence of the middle section must change the way the piece as a whole is perceived.

Unless is the abbreviated version of this piece.
